HIV prevention research ethics is a process of learning and unlearning that requires ongoing critical reflection on the part of the research community, the IRB, and the community.

the ethical challenges in HIV prevention research are not unique, but rather are the challenges faced in all research that must be addressed through a thoughtful application of ethical principles and practices.

ethical HIV prevention research requires the development of a research ethics framework that is sensitive to the needs of diverse communities.

the best way to promote ethical HIV prevention research is to involve the voices of those who are the subjects of research, and to ensure that the ethical review process is inclusive of the perspectives and values of the communities in which research is conducted.
